subs.scuola: The Scuola Grande of the Current

subs.basilica: The Basilica of the Serene Matron
subs.council: The Hall of the Great Council

routes.name: The Duke's Road
routes.text: The made road from Kesselhaven up to the castle and down to Ostwick, ditched and gravelled at the Duke's cost and tolled at his pleasure.

routes.name: The Levy Way
routes.text: The straight way the levy marches when the beacon is lit: no bends, no shade and no inns.

routes.name: The Wine Road
routes.text: Rutted by casks from Aschau to the harbour, and sticky under the wheels every autumn.

routes.name: The Abbey Way
routes.text: A quiet road between apple-trees, south to Pomerell. The brothers mend it themselves and count the stones.

routes.name: The Cider Lane
routes.text: The back way between the abbey's cider and the town's wine. Each end claims the other's drink is the cause of the potholes.

routes.name: The Beck Path
routes.text: It follows the beck from Ostwick down to the ford and up to the sheep-walls, and floods when the beck does.

routes.name: The Holly Lane
routes.text: A sunk lane between holly hedges, dark at noon and green all winter.

routes.name: The Beacon Path
routes.text: A footpath over the bald hill, kept clear so that a runner can find it in the dark.

routes.name: The Hanging Road
routes.text: The road to the forest, past the oak. Carters whistle on it, and not from cheerfulness.

routes.name: The Forest Rides
routes.text: Broad green rides cut for the Duke's hunt, mown by deer and policed by foresters.

routes.name: The Charcoal Road
routes.text: Black ruts from the Grauwald to the smelters. Nothing grows in the wheel-tracks.

routes.name: The Quarry Drag
routes.text: Worn hollow by stone-sledges, from the black quarry round the back of the crag.

routes.name: The Tourney Road
routes.text: The loop below the castle that fills with banners, farriers and pickpockets when the lists are open.

routes.name: The Common Paths
routes.text: Sheep-tracks over the common and the causeway through the reeds. They go where sheep would.

routes.name: The Oak Ways
routes.text: Old tracks under the oaks that were not made by the Duke and do not appear in his rolls.

routes.name: The High Tracks
routes.text: Goat-paths above the tree-line, marked by cairns and by the weather.

routes.name: The Ruin Tracks
routes.text: Paths between the mine and the old stones, kept open by people who would rather not say why.

routes.name: The Ferry Road
routes.text: East along the river to the rope-ferry and Luggen beyond, busy with drovers and slow with their beasts.

routes.name: The Salt Paths
routes.text: Plank-ways and firm ground through the Salzmoor, known to the salters and moved by the tide.

routes.name: The Streets of Kesselhaven
routes.text: Cobbles, gutters and handcarts, and somebody shouting the price of herring.

routes.name: The Tenn
routes.text: The duchy's river, from the castle crag down to the harbour. Barges go down on the current and are hauled back by oxen.

roadEvents.text: A carter going the other way calls the news without stopping: a ship in, a price up, a wedding off.
A ribbon on a thorn, new since yesterday. Someone has come this way with something to ask.
Rain comes over the hill all at once. You walk the next mile with your head down.
A ewe on the wrong side of a wall. You put her back. She is not grateful.
The Duke's riders come through at a canter, and the road stands aside for them.
Smoke hangs in the trees from a kiln you cannot see. The burners know you are here.
A spring by the way, cold enough to hurt your teeth.
A wandering priest of Pecutto, already cheerful, offers you the cup and a verse to go with it.
Mist off the water. For a while there is only the path under your feet.
The bargemen sing the same four lines from the castle to the sea.
A heron gets up from the shallows, slow as a man shaking out a cloak.
A drove of cattle fills the road from hedge to hedge. You wait, and eat their dust.

people.name: Hanne Brook
people.title: Farmhand of Ostwick
people.hint: a sunburnt young woman with a hayfork over her shoulder
people.meet: The young woman with the hayfork has been watching you work all week. “You’re not hopeless,” she says at last. “I’m Hanne. Come and have an ale when the light goes.”
talk: Hanne tells you which cows kick, which fields flood and which of the Brook cousins owes her money.
“One day I’ll have my own strip by the river,” Hanne says. “Barley. Nobody tells barley what to do.”

people.name: Jory Pell
people.title: Eel-Catcher of Kesselhaven
people.hint: a gnarled old man mending eel-traps
people.meet: The old eel-man spits, wipes his hand and holds it out. “Jory. Fifty years on this mole. You set a trap like a drunk priest, but you keep at it. I respect that.”
talk: Jory tells you the harbour was twice as deep when he was a boy, and the eels twice as long.
“Never eat an eel you didn’t kill yourself,” Jory says, and will not explain.

people.name: Mechthild Ambrosius
people.title: Poor Scholar of the Collegium
people.hint: an ink-stained woman asleep on a pile of books
people.meet: The ink-stained woman wakes, looks at what you are reading, and corrects your Allorese. “Mechthild. I’m writing a history of everything. Sit down, you’re in my light.”
talk: Mechthild has found a contradiction in the Collegium’s founding charter and is beside herself with joy.
“Nobody reads anymore,” Mechthild sighs, surrounded by four hundred people reading.

people.name: Zanetta Bon
people.title: Gondolier of Marre
people.hint: a gondolier singing as she rows
people.meet: The gondolier rests her oar. “You row like a Luggish barge, but you’re learning. Zanetta. Get in, I’ll show you the canals nobody shows foreigners.”
talk: Zanetta knows which palazzi have secret water-gates, and which families use them for what.
“Every gondolier in Marre is a spy for somebody,” Zanetta says. “I’m a spy for me.”

people.name: Bastian Caro
people.title: Silverer’s Apprentice of the Glass Isles
people.hint: a pale apprentice with silver on his fingertips
people.meet: The apprentice catches your reflection in a half-silvered glass and smiles at it, not at you. “You have a good reflection. I’m Bastian. Don’t tell the masters I spoke to you.”
talk: Bastian swears the Masque mirrors are just very good glass. He swears it a little too quickly.
“The Republic won’t let silverers leave the Isles,” Bastian says. “I’ve never wanted to. Mostly.”

people.name: Momolo Scarpa
people.title: Smuggler of Selino
people.hint: a lean man in a sailor’s cap who never sits with his back to the door
people.meet: The lean man slides onto the bench beside you. “The Cerdans have your description. That makes you interesting. Momolo. I know a boat.”
talk: Momolo knows every channel in the lagoon the customs boats can’t follow.
“Smuggling’s an honest trade,” Momolo says. “It’s the customs that’s the theft.”

people.name: Cateruccia Vio
people.title: Nurse of the Lazaretto
people.hint: a brisk nurse smelling of vinegar and juniper
people.meet: The nurse pushes a cup of vinegar-water at you. “Drink. You’ve been on the wards a week and you’re not dead, so you’re either lucky or careful. I’m Cateruccia. Be careful.”
talk: Cateruccia has nursed through three Pestilences and has a theory about each of them.
“The Prior says it’s seeds too small to see,” Cateruccia says. “I say it’s dirt. We both say wash your hands.”

people.name: Gerd Sack
people.title: Miller of Weirbeck
people.hint: a floury man with one shoulder higher than the other
people.meet: The miller looks at your hands before your face. “You can lift,” he says. “Good. I'm Gerd. Mind the stones.”
talk: Gerd tells you which farmers bring damp corn and hope he will not notice.
“A mill takes a sixteenth,” Gerd says. “Anyone who says I take more can turn the wheel himself.”

people.name: Alder Finch
people.title: Hayward of Netherwick
people.hint: a lean man walking the hedge with a billhook, counting gaps
people.meet: “Mind the gate,” says the man with the billhook, before anything else. Then, when you have minded it: “Alder Finch. Hayward. That means the hedges are my fault.”
talk: Alder can tell you whose cow got into whose corn, in what year, and what it cost.
“Hedges are law you can see,” Alder says.

people.name: Wilmar Tally
people.title: Clerk of the Tithe
people.hint: a neat young man with ink on his cuffs and a notched stick behind his ear
people.meet: “Name and holding,” says the clerk, without looking up. When you have neither, he looks up. “Wilmar. I count what is owed.”
talk: Wilmar explains the split tally: one half for the tenant, one for the Duke, and no arguing with wood.
“Everyone thinks the tenth is the sheaf I take,” Wilmar says. “It is the nine I leave.”

people.name: Old Nell Crook
people.title: Shepherd of the Common
people.hint: an old woman knitting as she walks, with two dogs that watch you instead of the sheep
people.meet: The old woman finishes her row before she speaks. “You'll be the new one. Nell. The dogs are Bit and Bother. Don't feed Bother.”
talk: Nell knows every ewe on the common by its face and most by its mother's.
“Sit facing the stone,” Nell says. “Never mind why. Your grandmother would have known.”

people.name: Lise Marsh
people.title: Goose-Girl of Dunmere
people.hint: a girl with a long switch and a flock that goes where she looks
people.meet: The geese reach you before she does. “They don't bite,” says the girl with the switch. “Well. That one bites. I'm Lise.”
talk: Lise drives forty geese to the castle kitchens every week and comes home with thirty-nine fewer.
“Geese know who is afraid of them,” Lise says. “So do I.”

people.name: Hob Wade
people.title: Keeper of the Ford
people.hint: a broad man standing in the water as if it were a road
people.meet: “Wait,” says the man in the water, and you wait while he reads the beck. “Now.” On the far side: “Hob. I say when.”
talk: Hob has pulled eleven carts, two friars and a bull out of the beck, and remembers the bull best.
“Water tells you everything,” Hob says, “just before it is too late.”

people.name: Berta Ash
people.title: Hearth-Keeper of the Cross
people.hint: a woman with soot to the elbows, feeding a fire one stick at a time
people.meet: She takes your stick, looks it over and lays it on. “Dry. Good. I'm Berta. The fire is older than the road.”
talk: Berta walks to the Ostwick shrine each week and carries a coal back in a clay pot.
“People think a hearth is kept by wood,” Berta says. “It is kept by coming back.”

people.name: Tom Russet
people.title: Picker of Sallowfield
people.hint: a long-armed man who looks at trees the way other men look at horses
people.meet: “That one will crop heavy,” says the long-armed man, nodding at a tree. Then at you: “Tom. You pick?”
talk: Tom knows the abbey's trees by their numbers and disagrees with the brothers about four of them.
“A ladder is only as good as its foot,” Tom says.

people.name: Kunz Hemp
people.title: The Duke's Hangman
people.hint: a quiet man mending a rope with a sailmaker's care
people.meet: He does not offer a hand. “Folk would rather not,” he says. “Kunz. I am paid by the Duke and thanked by nobody.”
talk: Kunz says a good knot is a kindness, and that he has never yet been asked what he thinks of a sentence.
“They cross the road to miss me,” Kunz says. “Then they send for me when a tooth wants pulling.”

people.name: Anke Dorn
people.title: Laundress to the Castle
people.hint: a red-armed woman who can tell a knight by his shirts
people.meet: “Whose are you?” she asks, and when you are nobody's: “Then you can carry. Anke. Those are the Duke's. Don't drop them.”
talk: Anke knows which knights are in debt, which are in love and which are ill, all from the linen.
“There are no secrets in a castle,” Anke says. “There is only washing.”

people.name: Dirk Hale
people.title: Host of the Broken Lance
people.hint: a grey man with a sergeant's voice and a limp he does not discuss
people.meet: “Sit,” says the host, in a voice that has moved pikemen. You sit. “Dirk. Served the Duke twenty years. Now I serve his squires, which is worse.”
talk: Dirk will tell you who unhorsed whom at any tourney for thirty years, and why it was the horse's fault.
“The lance over the fire is mine,” Dirk says. “The man who broke it paid for the inn.”

people.name: Jutta Lark
people.title: Lure-Maker of Falkenau
people.hint: a small woman stitching a leather lure, with a hawk asleep on the chair-back
people.meet: “Don't look her in the eye,” says the woman with the needle, meaning the hawk. “Jutta. She is Thistle. She is in a mood.”
talk: Jutta makes lures for the ducal mews and can tell you which of the Duke's birds will never be any good.
“A hawk does not love you,” Jutta says. “She agrees with you. For now.”

people.name: Bruno Slate
people.title: Quarryman
people.hint: a man the colour of his stone, with a maul over his shoulder
people.meet: He raps the rock and listens. “Sound,” he says, to the rock, and then to you: “Bruno. Stand there. Not there.”
talk: Bruno's grandfather cut the keep's gate-arch and was paid, the family says, in promises.
“Stone splits where it wants,” Bruno says. “The craft is in wanting the same.”

people.name: Mats Cole
people.title: Charcoal Carter
people.hint: a man black to the eyes, leading an ox that is black to the knees
people.meet: White teeth in a black face. “Don't shake hands,” he says. “Mats. You'll want to stand upwind.”
talk: Mats carries charcoal to the Silberhalde smelters and news back, and charges for neither.
“The forest burns slow or it burns fast,” Mats says. “We are the slow.”

people.name: Hilde Bracken
people.title: Forester of the Grauwald
people.hint: a woman in green and grey who was standing there some time before you saw her
people.meet: “You walk loud,” she says, from much nearer than you thought. “Hilde. The Duke's forester. That was not a complaint. It was a warning.”
talk: Hilde keeps the deer-count in her head and the roll only for the Duke's clerks.
“Poachers I can forgive,” Hilde says. “It is the ones who leave the snare that I hang.”

people.name: Wat Rush
people.title: Reed-Cutter
people.hint: a man in a punt, cutting without looking, with a pipe that is not lit
people.meet: The punt noses in. “Step in the middle,” he says, “or step in the mere.” When you are aboard: “Wat. I thatch half of Ostwick.”
talk: Wat sells thatch to the village and eels to the miller, and will not say what he sells to Mother Brindl.
“Reed grows back,” Wat says. “That is the whole of what I know, and it has fed me fifty years.”

people.name: Else Fold
people.title: Shearer of Steinwick
people.hint: a woman with forearms like a smith, sharpening shears on her boot
people.meet: “Hold that,” she says, and gives you a ewe. When the ewe has made its views known: “Else. You held on. That'll do.”
talk: Else can shear a ewe while it is still deciding whether to object.
“Wool is the only crop that walks to market,” Else says.

people.name: Henk Stave
people.title: Cooper
people.hint: a cheerful man rolling a cask with one foot while he talks
people.meet: The cask rolls up to your feet and stops. “Good, you can catch,” says the cooper. “Henk. That one leaks. Tell me where.”
talk: Henk makes the casks for Aschau's wine and says the wine is only as honest as the wood.
“A cask is a hundred mistakes you did not make,” Henk says.

people.name: Brother Otmar
people.title: Granger of Pomerell
people.hint: a monk with his sleeves tied back, talking to an ox as to a novice
people.meet: “He is called Patience,” says the monk, of the ox. “He is not. I am Brother Otmar, and I am learning it from him.”
talk: Brother Otmar keeps the grange accounts in the same book as the apple-trees, a page to each ox.
“The abbot prays for rain,” Otmar says. “I mend the roof.”

people.name: Old Rolf
people.title: Beacon-Ward
people.hint: an old soldier asleep sitting up, with one eye that opens before the other
people.meet: One eye opens. “I was not asleep,” says the old man. “I was listening. Rolf. I have lit that fire twice, and I would rather not a third time.”
talk: Rolf was a levy spearman and will show you the scar, whether or not you ask.
“A beacon is the Duke saying please,” Rolf says. “Loudly.”

activities.name: Carry sacks to the stones
activities.text: Up the ladder with a sack on your back, and down again for the next.

activities.name: Mow the haymead
activities.text: Scythe low, step, scythe low. Keep the line with the man beside you.

activities.name: Thresh with the flail
activities.text: Swing, turn the sheaf, swing. The rhythm matters more than the arm.

activities.name: Count the ewes at noon
activities.text: Every head on the common, twice, and the same number both times.

activities.name: Pluck down
activities.text: A goose under one arm, a sack under the other, and patience.

activities.name: Read the water
activities.text: Watch the stones, the colour and the speed, and say whether a cart may cross.

activities.name: Carry a coal for a traveller
activities.text: Bank it in ash in a clay pot, and bring it a mile down the road alive.

activities.name: Prune the outer trees
activities.text: Cut to the bud that faces out. Leave the tree room to breathe.

activities.name: Splice rope
activities.text: Unlay the strands, marry them, and tuck each one three times.

activities.name: Beat the linen
activities.text: Soap, stone and paddle, until the water runs clear.

activities.name: Walk the hot horses
activities.text: Round the yard at a slow walk until the steam is off them.

activities.name: Swing the lure
activities.text: A clean circle, a clean throw, and take it away before she binds to it.

activities.name: Dress a kerbstone
activities.text: Pitch, punch and point, until the face is true.

activities.name: Stack cordwood
activities.text: Four feet high, eight feet long, and tight enough that a squirrel cannot pass.

activities.name: Walk the forest bounds
activities.text: From marked oak to marked oak, noting every snare and every stump.

activities.name: Cut reed for thatch
activities.text: Sickle low to the water, bundle, tie and stack it in the punt.

activities.name: Mend a dry-stone wall
activities.text: Two over one, one over two, and a through-stone every yard.

activities.name: Raise a cask
activities.text: Staves in the hoop, fire inside, and bend them home before they cool.

activities.name: Yoke the oxen
activities.text: Bow under the neck, pin through the bow, and a word before you ask them to pull.

activities.name: Keep the beacon watch
activities.text: Eyes on the castle tower, and the flint dry.

activities.name: Plough a strip
activities.text: Walk the ox down your furrow and back, and keep the line the reeve can see.

activities.name: Sow the spring corn
activities.text: Seed from the apron, a handful to every third step.

activities.name: Weed the furrows
activities.text: Dock and thistle out by the root, strip after strip.

activities.name: Glean the stubble
activities.text: What the reapers dropped is yours, if you are quick.

activities.name: Drive the flock up
activities.text: Up the hill before the dew is off, with the dogs wide on either side.

activities.name: Watch the flock
activities.text: Sit where you can count them. Count them again.

activities.name: Tend the hives
activities.text: Smoke first, slow hands, and no talking near the skeps.

activities.name: Gather hill herbs
activities.text: Yarrow and thyme from the high side, cut while the dew holds.

activities.name: Bake the bread
activities.text: Fire the oven, shape the loaves, and mark yours with a thumb.

activities.name: Work the loom
activities.text: Shuttle and beat, shuttle and beat, a hand of cloth by noon.

activities.name: Brew small ale
activities.text: Mash, boil and cool, and keep the neighbours out of the wort.

activities.name: Hoe the onions
activities.text: Between the rows, shallow, before the sun is high.

activities.name: Water the plots
activities.text: Two pails from the well to every bed, in the cool of the evening.

activities.name: Serve the evening crowd
activities.text: Jugs out, pots back, and an ear for who owes whom.

activities.name: Roll at the kegel-alley
activities.text: Nine pins, three balls, and the loser fills the jug.

activities.name: Swap stories by the fire
activities.text: Yours for theirs. The ale-wife has heard both.

activities.name: Wrestle on the green
activities.text: Collar and elbow, best of three falls.

activities.name: Play for the green
activities.text: A reel to start with, and whatever they shout for after.

activities.name: Feed the village fire
activities.text: A log for the hearth that never goes out, and a word to Ilvara.

activities.name: Draw water at the well
activities.text: Rope, pail and a wet sleeve, four turns to the top.
